canonical_name: Weyl eigenvalue-inequality and perturbation family for finite Hermitian matrices
literal_source_claim_zh: Hermite矩阵特征值的扰动理论
literal_source_claim_en: Perturbation theory for eigenvalues of Hermitian matrices.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies a topic gloss, not a proposition. It does not select the upper additive Weyl family, its lower companion, their conjunction, or an operator-norm perturbation corollary; fix real symmetric versus complex Hermitian matrices, finite dimension, eigenvalue ordering and multiplicity, index arithmetic, norm, or zero-dimensional behavior. Weyl's inspected 1912 source states related inequalities for symmetric integral kernels in reciprocal Fredholm eigenparameter notation, not literally the catalog's finite complex Hermitian-matrix wording. Selecting an exact Lean proposition at intake would invent, broaden, narrow, or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix finite square real symmetric or complex Hermitian matrices, Nat/Fin or arbitrary finite index types, nonempty versus zero dimension, universes, and all Fintype/DecidableEq instances.
conclusion: Open: a source-selected upper or lower eigenvalue-of-sum inequality, conjunction of the additive family, endpoint bound, or indexed operator-norm perturbation estimate; exact eigenvalue enumeration, admissible indices, and norm are unresolved.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every boundary case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: for decreasing eigenvalues of n by n complex Hermitian A and B, lambda_(i+j-1)(A+B) <= lambda_i(A) + lambda_j(B) whenever i,j >= 1 and i+j-1 <= n
the lower companion lambda_(i+j-n)(A+B) >= lambda_i(A) + lambda_j(B) whenever i+j >= n+1
the conjunction of all admissible upper and lower Weyl inequalities
for each ordered eigenvalue, abs(lambda_i(A+B) - lambda_i(A)) <= operatorNorm(B)
equivalently, abs(lambda_i(A) - lambda_i(B)) <= operatorNorm(A-B) for two Hermitian matrices
the corresponding real symmetric matrix or finite-dimensional self-adjoint operator theorem
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero perturbation, zero matrix, scalar matrices, and commuting matrices
positive semidefinite, indefinite, and singular matrices
endpoint indices and every i+j off-by-one boundary
real symmetric versus complex Hermitian matrices
operator norm versus Frobenius, Schatten, entrywise, or another matrix norm
excluded_substitutions: Weyl's asymptotic eigenvalue law or criterion for essential spectrum
Weyl groups, Weyl chambers, root systems, or the Weyl character formula
singular-value Weyl inequalities or Hoffman-Wielandt bounds
Loewner monotonicity, Cauchy interlacing, Lidskii, Schur-Horn, or spectral variation alone
the spectral theorem, eigenvalue reality, or diagonalization without the selected inequality
normal, arbitrary nonsymmetric, infinite-dimensional, fixed-size, commuting-only, or numerical special cases
a hypothesis or structure storing the desired eigenvalue inequality
a floating-point eigensolver, sampled experiment, oracle, or unchecked certificate
the catalog's untrusted verified label, a source URL, or the discovery probe as proof credit
